[[Category: Cherry Fork Cemetery, Cherry Fork, Ohio]] 

== Biography ==
'''Robert Anderson Glasgow''' was a son of [[Glasgow-653|Joseph S. Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-876|Ann “Nancy” Glasgow]]. The 1880 county history identifies Robert A. as the second son of Joseph and Nancy and states that Joseph died in 1820 leaving his widow and eight children.<ref name="Adams1880">''Historical Sketch of Adams County, Ohio'', in ''Caldwell's Atlas of Adams County, 1797–1880'' (1880), p. 69, biographical sketch of Robert Anderson Glasgow; [https://www.ohiohistory.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Caldwell-s_Atlas_of_Adams_County_1797-1880.pdf digital copy].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Miami Valley family account ===

The memoir of [[Glasgow-2043|S. S. Glasgow]] places Robert A. in the same family as [[Glasgow-875|William B. Glasgow]], alongside Arthur and the married sisters. It supports the recent family identification while leaving the grandfather unnamed. Robert’s 1880 named-parent account remains the explicit Joseph/Nancy anchor; the memoir does not supply a new literal Joseph clause. <ref name="Miami1919">John C. Hover et al., eds., ''Memoirs of the Miami Valley'' (Robert O. Law Company, 1919–1920), “S. S. Glasgow,” printed pp. 257–258; [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18001/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 257] and [https://digital.cincinnatilibrary.org/iiif/2/p16998coll15:18002/full/full/0/default.jpg original p. 258], Cincinnati & Hamilton County Public Library Digital Library; images inspected 22 October 2026. Published family biography, not a civil or parish register.</ref>


=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-653]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The held 1880 Adams County biographical sketch explicitly calls Robert A. Glasgow the second son of Joseph and Nancy. His exact 1813 birth and family setting fit the selected Joseph household, yielding a specific named son attribution.

Confident 98%; explicit nineteenth-century biographical evidence, not a newly inspected parish or civil original.

Next useful test: Retain the county-history passage and compare family or probate records.

Source basis already held: [https://www.ohiohistory.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Caldwell-s_Atlas_of_Adams_County_1797-1880.pdf Historical Sketch of Adams County, Ohio, in Caldwell's Atlas of Adams County, 1797–1880 (1880), p. 69, biographical sketch of Robert Anderson Glasgow; digital copy (https://www.ohiohistory.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Caldwell-s_Atlas_of_Adams_County_1797-1880.pdf).]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
